1.1: The vision, either prophesy, of Isaiah, the son of Amoz, which he saw on Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, of Jotham, of Ahaz, and of Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
1.2: Ye heavens, hear, and thou earth, perceive with ears, for the Lord spake. I have nourished and I have enhanced sons; soothly they have despised me.
1.3: An ox knew his lord, and an ass knew the cratch of his lord; but Israel knew not me, and my people under-stood not.
1.4: Woe to the sinful folk, to the people heavy in wickedness, to the wayward seed, to the cursed sons; they have forsaken the Lord, they have blasphemed the Holy of Israel, they be alienated [[away]] backward.
1.5: On what thing shall I smite you more, that increase trespassing? Each head is sick, and each heart is mourning.
1.6: From the sole of the foot till to the noll, health is not therein; wound, and wanness, and beating swelling that is not bound about, neither cured by medicine, neither nursed with oil.
1.7: Your land is forsaken, your cities be burnt by fire; aliens devour your country before you, and it shall be desolate as in the destroying of enemies.
1.8: And the daughter of Zion, that is, Jerusalem, shall be forsaken as a shadowing place in a vineyard, and as an hulk in a place where gourds waxed, and as a city which is wasted.
1.9: If the Lord of hosts had not left seed to us, we had been as Sodom, and we had been like as Gomorrah.
1.10: Ye princes of men of Sodom, hear the word of the Lord; and ye people of Gomorrah, perceive with ears the law of your God.
1.11: Whereto offer ye to me [[or What to me]] the multitude of your sacrifices? saith the Lord. I am full; I would not the burnt sacrifices of wethers, and the inner fatness of fat beasts, and the blood of calves, and of lambs, and of bucks of goats.
1.12: When ye came before my sight, who asked of your hands these things, that ye should go in my foreyards?
1.13: Offer ye no more sacrifice in vain; incense is abomination to me; I shall not suffer new moon, and sabbath, and other feasts. For your companies be wicked;
1.14: my soul hateth your calends and your solemnities; those be dis-easeful to me, I travailed with suffering.
1.15: And when ye stretch forth your hands, I shall turn away mine eyes from you; and when ye multiply prayer, I shall not hear; for why your hands be full of blood.
1.16: Be ye washed, be ye clean; do ye away the evil of your thoughts from mine eyes; cease ye to do waywardly,
1.17: learn ye to do well. Seek ye doom, help ye him that is oppressed, deem ye to the fatherless and motherless child, defend ye a widow.
1.18: And come ye, and prove ye me, saith the Lord. Though your sins be as blood-red, those shall be made white as snow; and though they be red as vermilion, they shall be white as wool.
1.19: If ye will, and hear me, ye shall eat the goods of [[the]] earth.
1.20: That if ye do not, and ye stir me to wrathfulness [[or wrath]], sword shall devour you; for why the mouth of the Lord spake.
1.21: How is the faithful city full of doom made an whore? rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]] dwelled therein; but now men-quellers dwell therein.
1.22: Thy silver is turned into dross, either filth; thy wine is meddled [[or mingled]] with water.
1.23: Thy princes be unfaithful, the fellows of thieves; all love gifts, and follow yieldings, either meeds; they deem not to a fatherless child, and the cause of a widow entereth not to them.
1.24: For this thing, saith the Lord God of hosts, the Strong of Israel, Alas! I shall be comforted on mine enemies, and I shall be avenged of mine enemies.
1.25: And I shall turn mine hand to thee, and I shall seethe out thy filth to the clean, and I shall do away all thy tin.
1.26: And I shall restore thy judges, as they were before, and thy counsellors, as in eld [[or old]] time. After these things thou shalt be called the city of the rightful [[or rightwise]], a faithful city.
1.27: Zion shall be again-bought in doom, and they shall bring it again into rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]];
1.28: and God shall all-break [[the]] cursed men and [[the]] sinners together, and they that forsake the Lord, shall be wasted.
1.29: For they shall be ashamed of [[the]] idols, to which they made sacrifice; and ye shall be ashamed on the orchards, which ye choosed.
1.30: When ye shall be as an oak, when the leaves fall down, and as an orchard without water.
1.31: And your strength shall be as a dead spark of stubble, either of hards of flax, and your work shall be as a quick spark; and ever either shall be burnt together, and none shall be that shall quench.

2.1: The word which Isaiah, the son of Amoz, saw on Judah and Jerusalem.
2.2: And in the last days the hill of the house of the Lord shall be made ready in the top of hills [[or the mountains]], and shall be raised above little hills. And all heathen men shall flow to him;
2.3: and many peoples shall go, and shall say, Come ye, ascend we [[or go we up]] to the hill of the Lord, and to the house of God of Jacob; and he shall teach us his ways, and we shall go in the paths of him. For why the law shall go out of Zion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.
2.4: And he shall deem heathen men, and he shall reprove many peoples; and they shall weld together their swords into shares, and their spears into sickles, either scythes; folk shall no more raise sword against folk, and they shall no more be exercised, either haunted, to battle.
2.5: Come ye, the house of Jacob, and go we in the light of the Lord.
2.6: Forsooth thou hast cast away thy people, the house of Jacob, for they be [[full-]]filled as sometime before; and they had false diviners by the chittering of birds, as Philistines, and they cleaved to alien children.
2.7: The land is filled with silver and gold, and none end is of the treasures thereof; and the land thereof is filled with horses, and the four-horsed carts thereof be unnumberable.
2.8: And the land thereof is filled with idols, and they worship the work of their hands, which their fingers made;
2.9: and a man bowed himself, and a man of full age was made low. Therefore forgive thou not to them.
2.10: Enter thou, people of Judah, into a stone, be thou hid in a ditch in earth, from the face of the dread of the Lord, and from the glory of his majesty.
2.11: The eyes of an high man be made low, and the highness of men shall be bowed down; forsooth the Lord alone shall be enhanced in that day.
2.12: For the day of the Lord of hosts shall be on each proud man and high, and on each boaster, and he shall be made low;
2.13: and on all the cedars of the Lebanon high and raised, and on all the oaks of Bashan,
2.14: and on all high mountains, and on all little hills, that be raised [[up]];
2.15: and on each high tower, and on each strong wall;
2.16: and on all [[the]] ships of Tarshish, and on all thing which is fair in sight.
2.17: And all the highness of men shall be bowed down, and the highness of men shall be made low; and the Lord alone shall be raised [[up]] in that day,
2.18: and idols shall be broken altogether utterly.
2.19: And they shall enter into the dens of stones, and into the swallows of [[the]] earth, from the face of the inward dread of the Lord, and from the glory of his majesty, when he shall rise to smite the land.
2.20: In that day a man shall cast away the idols of his silver, and the simulacra of his gold, which he had made to himself, for to worship mouldwarps and bats.
2.21: And he shall enter into [[the]] chinks, either crazings, of stones, and into the caves of hard rocks, from the face of the inward dread of the Lord, and from the glory of his majesty, when he shall rise to smite the land.
2.22: Therefore cease ye from a man, whose spirit is in his nostrils, for he is areckoned high.

3.1: For lo! the lordly governor, the Lord of hosts, shall take away from Jerusalem and from Judah a mighty man, and strong, and all the strength of bread, and all the strength of water;
3.2: a strong man, and a man a warrior, and a doomsman, and a prophet, and a false diviner in altars, and an eld [[or old]] man,
3.3: a prince over fifty men, and a worshipful man in cheer, and a counsellor, and a wise man of principal craftsmen, and a prudent man of mystic, either ghostly, speech.
3.4: And I shall give children to be the princes of them, and men of women’s conditions shall be lords of them.
3.5: And the people shall fall down, a man to a man, each man to his neighbour; a child shall make noise against an eld [[or old]] man, and an unnoble man against a noble man.
3.6: For a man shall take his brother, the menial of his father, and shall say, A cloth is to thee, be thou our prince; forsooth this falling be under thine hand.
3.7: And he shall answer in that day, and say, I am no leech, and neither bread, neither cloth is in mine house; do not ye make me prince of the people.
3.8: For why Jerusalem fell down, and Judah fell down altogether; for the tongue of them, and the findings of them, were against the Lord, for to stir to wrath the eyes of his majesty.
3.9: The knowing of their cheer hall answer to them; and they preached their sin, as Sodom did, and hid not. Woe to the soul of them, for why evils be yielded to them.
3.10: Say ye to the just [[or rightwise]] man, that it shall be to him well; for he shall eat the fruit of his findings.
3.11: Woe to the wicked man into evil; for why the yielding of his hands shall be made to him.
3.12: The wrongful askers of my people robbed it, and women were lords thereof. My people, they that say thee blessed, deceive thee, and destroy the way of thy steps.
3.13: The Lord standeth for to deem, and he standeth for to deem [[the]] peoples;
3.14: the Lord shall come to doom, with the elder men of his people, and with his princes; for ye have wasted my vineyard, and the raven of a poor man is in your house.
3.15: Why all-break ye my people, and grind together the faces of poor men? saith the Lord God of hosts.
3.16: And the Lord God said, For that that the daughters of Zion were raised, and went with neck stretched forth, and went by signs of eyes, and clapped with hands, and went, and with their feet went in well-arrayed going,
3.17: the Lord shall make bald the noll of the daughters of Zion, and the Lord shall make naked the hair of them.
3.18: In that day the Lord shall take away the ornament of shoes, and golden little bells like the moon,
3.19: and ribbons, and brooches, and ornaments of arms nigh the shoulders,
3.20: and mitres, either chaplets, and combs, and ornaments of arms nigh the hands, and golden ornaments like lampreys, and little vessels of ointments, and earrings,
3.21: and rings, and precious stones hanging in the forehead,
3.22: and changing clothes, and mantles, and sheets, either smocks, and needles [[or pins]],
3.23: and mirrors, and small linen clothes about the shoulders, and kerchiefs, and rochets.
3.24: And stink shall be for sweet odour, and a cord for the girdle; baldness shall be for the crisp hair, and an hair-shirt for a breast-girdle.
3.25: Also thy fairest men shall fall by sword, and thy strong men shall fall in battle.
3.26: And the gates thereof shall wail, and mourn; and it shall sit desolate in [[the]] earth.

4.1: And seven women shall catch one man in that day, and shall say, We shall eat our bread, and we shall be covered with our clothes; only thy name be called on us, do thou away our shame.
4.2: In that day the burgeoning of the Lord shall be in great worship and glory; and the fruit of [[the]] earth shall be high, and full out joy to them that shall be saved of Israel.
4.3: And it shall be, each that is left in Zion, and is residue in Jerusalem, shall be called holy; each that is written in life in Jerusalem;
4.4: for the Lord washeth away the filths of the daughters of Zion, and washeth the blood of Jerusalem from the midst thereof, in the spirit of doom, and in the spirit of heat.
4.5: And the Lord made on each place of the hill of Zion, and where he was called to help, a cloud by day, and smoke, and brightness of fire flaming in the night; for why covering, either defending, shall be above all glory.
4.6: And a tabernacle shall be into a shadowing place of the day, from heat, and into secureness, and into hiding, from whirlwind and from rain.

5.1: I shall sing for my darling the song of mine uncle’s son, of his vineyard. A vinery [[or vineyard]] was made to my darling, in the horn, that is, in an high place and excellent, in the son of oil, that is, in a place full of olives, of whose fruit is wrung out oil.
5.2: And he hedged it, and chose stones thereof, and planted a chosen vinery [[or vineyard]]; and he builded a tower in the midst thereof, and reared a wine press therein; and he abode, that it should make grapes, and it made wild grapes.
5.3: Now therefore, ye dwellers of Jerusalem, and ye men of Judah, deem between me and my vinery [[or vineyard]].
5.4: What is it that I ought to do more to my vinery [[or vineyard]], and I did not to it? whether that I abode, that it should make grapes, and it made wild grapes?
5.5: And now I shall show to you, what I shall do to my vinery [[or vineyard]]. I shall take away the hedge thereof, and it shall be into ravishing; I shall cast down the wall thereof, and it shall be into defouling;
5.6: and I shall set it deserted, either forsaken. It shall not be cut, and it shall not be digged, and briars and thorns shall grow upon it; and I shall command to [[the]] clouds, that they rain not rain on it.
5.7: Forsooth the vinery [[or vineyard]] of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah be the delightable burgeoning of him. I abode, that it shall make doom, and lo! wickedness; and that it should do rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]], and lo! cry.
5.8: Woe to you that join house to house, and couple field to field, till to the end of [[a]] place. Whether ye alone shall dwell in the midst of the land?
5.9: These things be in the ears of me, the Lord of hosts; If many houses be not forsaken, great and fair, without dweller, believe ye not to me.
5.10: For why ten acres of vines [[or vineyards]] shall make one pottle, and thirty bushels of seed shall make three bushels.
5.11: Woe to you that rise altogether early to follow drunkenness, and to drink till to eventide, that ye burn with wine.
5.12: Harp, and gittern, and tympan, and pipe, and wine be in your feasts; and ye behold not the work of the Lord, neither ye behold the works of his hands.
5.13: Therefore my people is led captive, either prisoner, for it had not knowing; and the noblemen thereof perished in hunger, and the multitude thereof was dry in thirst.
5.14: Therefore hell hath alarged his soul, and opened his mouth without any end; and the strong men thereof, and the people thereof, and the high men, and the glorious men thereof, shall go down to it.
5.15: And a man shall be bowed down, and a man of age shall be made low; and the eyes of high men shall be pressed down.
5.16: And the Lord of hosts shall be enhanced in doom, and [[the]] holy God shall be hallowed in rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]].
5.17: And lambs shall be fed by their order, and comelings shall eat of the desert places turned into plenty.
5.18: Woe to you that draw wickedness in the cords of vanity, and draw sin as the bond of a wain;
5.19: and ye say, The work of him hasten, and come soon, that we see; and the counsel of the Holy of Israel nigh, and come, and we shall know it.
5.20: Woe to you that say evil good, and good evil; and put darknesses light, and light darknesses; and put bitter thing into sweet, and sweet thing into bitter.
5.21: Woe to you that be wise men in your eyes, and be prudent before yourselves.
5.22: Woe to you that be mighty to drink wine, and be strong to meddle [[or mingle]] drunkenness;
5.23: and ye justify a wicked man for gifts, and ye take away the rightful-ness [[or rightwiseness]] of a just [[or rightwise]] man from him.
5.24: For this thing, as the tongue of fire devoureth stubble, and the heat of flame burneth, so the root of them shall be as a dead spark, and the seed of them shall ascend [[or go up]] as dust; for they casted away the law of the Lord of hosts, and blasphemed the speech of the Holy of Israel.
5.25: Therefore the strong vengeance of the Lord was wroth against his people, and he stretched forth his hand on it, and smote it; and hills were troubled [[or the mountains be disturbed]], and the dead bodies of them were made as a turd in the midst [[or the middle]] of streets. In all these things the strong vengeance of him was not turned away, but yet his hand was stretched forth.
5.26: And he shall raise [[up]] a sign among nations afar, and he shall hiss to him from the ends of [[the]] earth; and lo! he shall hasten, and shall come swiftly.
5.27: None is failing neither travailing in that host; he shall not nap, neither sleep, neither the girdle of his reins shall be undone, neither the lace of his shoe shall be broken.
5.28: His arrows be sharp, and all his bows be bent; the hoofs of his horses be as flint, and his wheels be as the fierceness of tempest.
5.29: His roaring shall be as of a lion; he shall roar as the whelps of lions; and he shall gnash, and shall hold prey, and shall embrace, and none shall be, that shall deliver.
5.30: And he shall sound on it in that day, as doeth the sound of the sea; we shall behold into the earth, and lo! darknesses of tribulation, and light is made dark in the darkness thereof.

6.1: In the year in which the king Uzziah was dead, I saw the Lord sitting on an high seat, and raised [[up]]; and the house of the Lord was full of his majesty, and those things that were under him filled the temple.
6.2: Seraphim stood [[up]] on it, six wings were to one, and six wings to the other; with two wings they covered the face of him, and with two wings they covered the feet of him, and with two wings they flew.
6.3: And they cried the one to the tother, and said, Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God of hosts; all [[the]] earth is full of his glory.
6.4: And the lintels above of the hinges were moved altogether of the voice of the crier, and the house of the Lord was filled with smoke.
6.5: And I said, Woe to me, for I was still; for I am a man defouled in lips, and I dwell in the midst of the people having defouled lips, and I saw with mine eyes the King, Lord of hosts.
6.6: And one of [[the]] seraphim flew to me, and a burning coal was in his hand, which coal he had taken with a tong from the altar.
6.7: And he touched my mouth, and said, Lo! I have touched thy lips with this coal, and thy wickedness shall be done away, and thy sin shall be cleansed.
6.8: And I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who shall go to you? And I said, Lo! I; send thou me.
6.9: And he said, Go thou, and thou shalt say to this people, Ye hearing hear, and ye do not understand; and see ye the prophesy, and do not ye know.
6.10: Make thou blind the heart of this people, and aggrieve thou the ears thereof, and close thou the eyes thereof; lest peradventure it see with his eyes, and hear with his ears, and understand with his heart, and it be converted, and I make it whole.
6.11: And I said, Lord, how long? And he said, Till [[the]] cities be made desolate, without dweller, and houses without man. And the land shall be left desert,
6.12: and the Lord shall make men afar. And that that was forsaken in the middle of [[the]] earth, shall be multiplied,
6.13: and yet the tithing, either tenth part, shall be therein; and it shall be converted, and it shall be into showing, as a terebinth is, and as an oak, that spreadeth abroad his boughs; that shall be holy seed, that shall stand therein.

7.1: And it was done in the days of Ahaz, the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin, the king of Syria, and Pekah, the son of Remaliah, the king of Israel, ascended [[or went up]] to Jerusalem, for to fight against it; and they might not overcome it.
7.2: And they told to the house of David, and said, Syria hath rested on Ephraim, that is, the king of Syria and the king of Israel be confederated, to come together against the realm of Judah, and the heart of him and of his people was moved altogether, as the trees of woods be moved of the face of the wind.
7.3: And the Lord said to Isaiah, Go thou out, and Jashub, thy son, which is left, into the meeting of Ahaz, at the last end of the water conduit of the higher cistern, in the way of the field of the fuller.
7.4: And thou shalt say to him, See thou, that thou be still; do not thou dread, and thine heart be not afeared of the two tails of these brands smoking, in the wrath of the strong vengeance of Rezin, king of Syria, and of the son of Remaliah.
7.5: For Syria, and Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah, have begun evil counsel against thee, and say,
7.6: Go we up to Judah, and raise we him, and draw we him out to us; and set we a king in the midst thereof, the son of Tabeal.
7.7: The Lord God saith these things, This shall not be, and it shall not stand;
7.8: but Damascus shall be the head of Syria, and Rezin shall be the head of Damascus; and yet sixty years and five, and Ephraim shall fail to be a people;
7.9: and Samaria shall fail to be the head of Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah to be [[the]] head of Samaria. Forsooth if ye shall not believe, ye shall not dwell.
7.10: And the Lord added to speak to Ahaz, and said,
7.11: Ask thou to thee a sign of thy Lord God, into the depth of hell, either into [[the]] height above.
7.12: And Ahaz said, I shall not ask, and I shall not tempt the Lord.
7.13: And Isaiah said, Therefore the house of David, hear ye; whether it is little to you to be dis-easeful to men, for ye be dis-easeful also to my God?
7.14: For this thing the Lord himself shall give a sign to you. Lo! a virgin shall conceive, and shall bear a son; and his name shall be called Immanuel. [[For that he the Lord shall give to you a token. Behold! a maiden shall conceive, and bare a son; and thou shalt call his name Immanuel.]]
7.15: He shall eat butter and honey, that he know how to reprove evil, and choose good.
7.16: For why before the child know how to reprove evil, and choose good, the land, which thou loathest, shall be forsaken of the face of their two kings.
7.17: The Lord shall bring on thee, and on thy people, and on the house of thy father, days that came not from the days of [[the]] departing of Ephraim from Judah, with the king of Assyrians.
7.18: And it shall be, in that day the Lord shall hiss to a fly, which is in the last part of the floods of Egypt; and to a bee, which is in the land of Assur;
7.19: and all those shall come, and shall rest in the strands [[or streams]] of valleys, and in the caves of stones, and in all [[the]] places of bushes, and in all holes.
7.20: And in that day the Lord shall shave with a sharp razor in these men, that be beyond the flood, of the king of Assyrians, the head, and the hairs of the feet, and all the beard.
7.21: And it shall be, in that day, a man shall nourish a cow of oxes, and two sheep,
7.22: and for the plenty of milk he shall eat butter; for why each man that shall be left in the midst of the land, shall eat butter and honey.
7.23: And it shall be, in that day each place where a thousand vineries [[or vines]] shall be worth a thousand pieces of silver, and shall be into thorns and briars,
7.24: men shall enter thither with bows and arrows; for why briars and thorns shall be in all the land.
7.25: And all hills that shall be purged with a briar hook, the dread of thorns and of briars shall not come thither; and it shall be into pasture of oxen, and into the treading of sheep.

8.1: And the Lord said to me, Take to thee a great book, and write therein with the pointel or stylus of man, Swiftly draw thou away spoils, take thou prey soon.
8.2: And I gave to me faithful witnesses, Uriah, the priest, and Zechariah, the son of Jeberechiah.
8.3: And I nighed to the prophetess; and she conceived, and childed a son. And the Lord said to me, Call thou his name, Haste thou to draw away spoils, haste thou for to take prey.
8.4: For why before that the child know how to call his father and his mother, the strength of Damascus shall be done away, and the spoils of Samaria, before the king of Assyrians.
8.5: And the Lord added to speak yet to me, and he said,
8.6: For that thing that this people hath cast away the waters of Shiloah, that go with silence, and hath taken more [[to]] Rezin, and the son of Remaliah,
8.7: for this thing lo! the Lord shall bring [[up]] on them the strong and many waters of the flood, the king of Assyrians, and all his glory; and he shall ascend [[or go up]] on all the streams thereof, and he shall flow on all the rivers thereof.
8.8: And he shall go flowing by Judah, and he shall pass till to the neck, and shall come; and the spreading forth of his wings shall be, and shall fill the breadth of thy land, thou Immanuel.
8.9: Peoples, be ye gathered together, and be ye overcome; and all lands afar, hear ye. Be ye comforted, and be ye overcome; gird ye you, and be ye overcome;
8.10: take ye counsel, and it shall be destroyed; speak ye a word, and it shall not be done, for God is with us.
8.11: For why the Lord saith these things to me, as he taught me in a strong hand, that I should not go into the way of this people, and said,
8.12: Say ye not, It is swearing together, for why all things which this people speaketh is swearing together; and dread ye not the fearedfulness thereof, neither be ye afeared.
8.13: Hallow ye the Lord himself of hosts; and he shall be your inward dread, and he shall be your feared-fulness, and he shall be to you into hallowing.
8.14: Forsooth he shall be into a stone of hurting, and into a stone of stumbling, to twain [[or the two]] houses of Israel; into a snare, and into falling, to them that dwell in Jerusalem.
8.15: And full many of them shall stumble, and shall fall, and they shall be all-broken, and they shall be bound, and shall be taken.
8.16: Bind thou [[the]] witnessing, mark thou the law in my disciples.
8.17: I shall abide the Lord, that hath hid his face from the house of Jacob, and I shall abide him.
8.18: Lo! I and my children, which the Lord gave to me into a sign, and great wonder to Israel, of the Lord of hosts that dwelleth in the hill of Zion.
8.19: And when they say to you, Ask ye of conjurers, and of false diviners, that gnash in their enchantings, whether the people shall not ask of their God a revelation, for quick men and [[the]] dead?
8.20: It is to go to the law more rather, and to the witnessing, that if they say not after this word, morrowtide light shall not be to them.
8.21: And it shall pass by that, and it shall fall down, and it shall hunger. And when it shall hunger, it shall be wroth, and shall curse his king and his God, and it shall behold upward.
8.22: And it shall look to the earth, and lo! tribulation, and darknesses, and unbinding, either discomfort, and anguish, and mist pursuing; and it shall not be able to flee away from his anguish.

9.1: In the first time, the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali was alighted, either released; and at the last, the way of the sea beyond Jordan, of Galilee of heathen men, was made heavy.
9.2: The people that went in darknesses saw a great light; when men dwelled in the country of [[the]] shadow of death, light rose up to them.
9.3: Thou multipliedest folk, thou magnifiedest not gladness; they shall be glad before thee, as they that be glad in harvest, as overcomers make full out joy, when they have taken a prey, when they part the spoils.
9.4: For thou hast overcome the yoke of his burden, and the rod of his shoulder, and the sceptre of his wrongful asker, as in the day of Midian.
9.5: For why all violent raven with noise, and a cloth meddled [[or mingled]] with blood, shall be into burning, and the meat of fire.
9.6: Forsooth a little child is born to us, and a son is given to us, and prince-hood is made [[up]] on his shoulder; and his name shall be called Wonderful, A counsellor, God, Strong, Father of the world to coming, A prince of peace, [[or Marvellous, Counsellor, God, Strong, Father of the world to come, Prince of peace]].
9.7: His empire shall be multiplied, and none end shall be of his peace; he shall sit on the seat of David, and on the realm of him, that he confirm it, and make strong in doom and rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]], from henceforth and till into without end. The fervent love of the Lord of hosts shall make this.
9.8: The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it fell in Israel.
9.9: And all the people of Ephraim shall know, and they that dwell in Samaria, saying in the pride and greatness of heart,
9.10: Tilestones fell down, but we shall build with square stones; they have cut down sycamores, but we shall change to cedars.
9.11: And the Lord shall raise the enemies of Rezin on him, and he shall turn the enemies of him into noise;
9.12: God shall make Syria to come from the east, and Philistines from the west; and with all the mouth they shall devour Israel. In all these things the strong vengeance of the Lord is not turned away, but yet his hand is stretched forth;
9.13: and the people is not turned again to the Lord smiting it, and they sought not the Lord of hosts.
9.14: And the Lord shall lose from Israel the head and the tail, [[the]] crooking and [[the]] beshrewing, either refraining, in one day.
9.15: An eld man and honourable, he is the head; and a prophet teaching leasing, he is the tail.
9.16: And they that bless his people, shall be deceivers, and they that be blessed, shall be cast down.
9.17: For this thing the Lord shall not be glad on the young men thereof, and he shall not have mercy on the fatherless children and widows thereof; for each man is an hypocrite and wayward, and each mouth spake folly. In all these things the strong vengeance of him is not turned away, but yet his hand is stretched forth; and the people is not turned again to the Lord smiting it.
9.18: For why wickedness is kindled as fire; it shall devour the briars and thorns, and it shall be kindled in the thickness of the forest, and it shall be wrapped altogether in the pride of smoke.
9.19: In the wrath of the Lord of hosts the land shall be troubled, and the people shall be as the meat of fire; a man shall not spare his brother.
9.20: And he shall bow to the right half, and he shall hunger, and he shall eat at the left half, and he shall not be [[ful]] filled; each man shall devour the flesh of his arm.
9.21: Manasseh shall devour Ephraim, and Ephraim shall devour Manasseh, and they together against Judah. In all these things the strong vengeance of him is not turned away, but yet his hand is stretched forth.

10.1: Woe to them that make wicked laws, and they writing have written unrightfulness [[or unrightwiseness]],
10.2: for to oppress poor men in doom, and to do violence to the cause of meek men of my people; that widows shall be the prey of them, and that they should ravish fatherless children.
10.3: What shall ye do in the day of visitation, and of wretchedness coming from [[a]] far? To whose help shall ye flee? and where shall ye leave your glory,
10.4: that ye be not bowed down under bond, and fall not down with slain men? On all these things his strong vengeance is not turned away, but yet his hand is stretched forth.
10.5: Woe to Assur, he is the rod and staff of my strong vengeance; mine indignation is in the hand of them.
10.6: I shall send him to a false folk, and I shall command to him against the people of my strong vengeance; that he take away the spoils, and part prey, and that he set [[or put]] that people into defouling, as the fen of streets.
10.7: Forsooth he shall not deem so, and his heart shall not guess so, but his heart shall be for to all-break, and to the slaying of many folks.
10.8: For he shall say, Whether my princes be not kings altogether?
10.9: Whether not as Carchemish, so Calno; and as Arpad, so Hamath? whether not as Damascus, so Samaria?
10.10: As mine hand found the realms of idols, so and the simulacra of them of Jerusalem and of Samaria.
10.11: Whether not as I did to Samaria, and to the idols thereof, so I shall do to Jerusalem, and to the simulacra thereof?
10.12: And it shall be, when the Lord hath [[ful]] filled all his works in the hill [[or the mount]] of Zion and in Jerusalem, I shall visit on the fruit of the great doing heart of the king of Assur, and on the glory of the highness of his eyes.
10.13: For he said, I have done in the strength of mine hand, and I have understood in my wisdom; and I have taken away the ends of [[the]] peoples, and I have robbed the princes of them, and I as a mighty man have drawn down them that sat on high.
10.14: And mine hand found the strength of peoples as a nest, and as eggs be gathered together that be forsaken, so I gathered together all [[the]] earth; and none there was that moved a feather, and opened the mouth, and grutched.
10.15: Whether an ax shall have glory against him that cutteth with it? either a saw shall be enhanced against him of whom it is drawn? as if a rod is raised against him that raiseth it, and a staff is enhanced, which soothly is a tree.
10.16: For this thing the lordly governor, Lord of hosts, shall send thinness into the fat men of him; and his glory kindled under shall burn as the burning of fire.
10.17: And the light of Israel shall be in fire, and the Holy of it in flame; and the thorn of him and briar shall be kindled and devoured in one day.
10.18: And the glory of his forest, and of his Carmel, shall be wasted, from the soul unto [[the]] flesh; and he shall be fleeing away for dread.
10.19: And the remnants of the trees of his forest shall be numbered for fewness, and a child shall write them.
10.20: And it shall be in that day, the remnant of Israel, and they that fled of the house of Jacob, shall not add for to trust on him that smiteth them; but it shall trust on the holy Lord of Israel, in truth.
10.21: The remnants, I say, the remnants of Jacob, shall be converted to the strong Lord.
10.22: For why, Israel, if thy people is as the gravel of the sea, the remnants shall be turned thereof; an ending made short shall make rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]] to be plenteous.
10.23: For why the Lord God of hosts shall make an ending and abridging, in the midst of all earth.
10.24: For this thing the Lord God of hosts saith these things, My people, the dweller of Zion, do not thou dread of Assur, for he shall smite thee in a rod, and he shall raise [[up]] his staff on thee in the way of Egypt.
10.25: For why yet a little, and a little, and mine indignation and my strong vengeance shall be ended on the great trespass of them.
10.26: And the Lord of hosts shall raise [[up]] a scourge on him by the vengeance of Midian in the stone of Oreb, and by his rod on the sea; and he shall raise that rod in the way of Egypt.
10.27: And it shall be in that day, his burden shall be taken away from thy shoulder, and his yoke from thy neck; and the yoke shall wax [[all]] rotten from the face of oil.
10.28: He shall come into Aiath, he shall pass into Migron, at Michmash he shall betake his vessels to keeping.
10.29: They passed swiftly, Geba is our seat, Ramah was astonied, Gibeah of Saul fled.
10.30: Thou daughter of Gallim, wail with thy voice; thou Laish, perceive, thou poor Anathoth.
10.31: Madmenah passed; the dwellers of Gebim fled; be ye comforted.
10.32: Yet it is the day, that men stand in Nob; he shall drive his hand on the hill [[or the mount]] of the daughter of Zion, on the little hill of Jerusalem.
10.33: Lo! the Lordly Governor, the Lord of hosts, shall break a pottle in dread, and high men of stature shall be cut down. And proud men shall be made low,
10.34: and the thick things of the forest shall be destroyed by iron; and the Lebanon with high things shall fall down.

11.1: And a rod shall go out of the root of Jesse, and a flower shall ascend [[or go up]] of the root of it.
11.2: And the Spirit of the Lord shall rest on him, the spirit of wisdom and of understanding, the spirit of counsel and of strength, the spirit of knowing and of piety;
11.3: and the spirit of the dread of the Lord shall fill him. He shall deem not by the sight of eyes, neither he shall reprove, either convict, by the hearing of ears;
11.4: but he shall deem in rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]] poor men, and he shall reprove in equity, for the mild men of [[the]] earth. And he shall smite the land with the rod of his mouth, and with the spirit of his lips he shall slay the wicked man.
11.5: And rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]] shall be the girdle of his loins, and faith shall be the girding of his reins.
11.6: A wolf shall dwell with a lamb, and a leopard shall rest with a kid; a calf, and a lion, and a sheep shall dwell together, and a little child shall drive them.
11.7: A calf and a bear shall be pastured together; the whelps of them shall rest together, and a lion as an ox shall eat straw.
11.8: And a young sucking child from the teat shall delight on the hole of a snake, and he that is weaned shall put his hand in the cave of the cockatrice.
11.9: They shall not annoy, and shall not slay, in all mine holy hill [[or holy mountain]]; for why the earth is filled with the knowing of the Lord, as [[the]] waters of the sea covering.
11.10: In that day the root of Jesse, that standeth into the sign of peoples; heathen men shall beseech him, and his sepulchre shall be glorious.
11.11: And it shall be in that day, the Lord shall add the second time his hand to have in possession the residue of his people that shall be left, of [[the]] Assyrian, and of Egypt, and of Pathros, and of Ethiopia, and of Elam, and of Shinar, and of Hamath, and of [[the]] isles of the sea.
11.12: And he shall raise a sign to nations, and shall gather together the fleers-away of Israel; and he shall gather together the scattered men of Judah from [[the]] four coasts of [[the]] earth.
11.13: And the envy of Ephraim shall be done away, and the enemies of Judah shall perish; Ephraim shall not have envy to Judah, and Judah shall not fight against Ephraim.
11.14: And they shall fly into the shoulders of Philistines by the sea, they shall take prey together of the sons of the east; Idumea and Moab shall be under the commandment of the hand of them, and the sons of Ammon shall be obedient.
11.15: And the Lord shall make desolate the tongue of the sea of Egypt, and he shall raise his hand on the flood in the strength of his spirit; and he shall smite, either part, it into seven rivers, so that shod men pass by it.
11.16: And a way shall be to my residue people that shall be left, of the Assyrians, as it was to Israel, in the day in which it ascended [[or went up]] from the land of Egypt.

12.1: And thou shalt say in that day, Lord, I shall acknowledge to thee, for thou were wroth to me; thy strong vengeance is turned, and thou hast comforted me.
12.2: Lo! God is my saviour, I shall do faithfully, and I shall not dread. For why the Lord is my strength and my praising, and he is made to me into health.
12.3: Ye shall draw waters with joy of the wells of the saviour.
12.4: And ye shall say in that day, Acknowledge ye to the Lord, and call ye his name into help; make ye known his findings among peoples; have ye mind, that his name is high.
12.5: Sing ye to the Lord, for he hath done worshipfully; tell ye this [[out]] in all [[the]] earth.
12.6: Thou dwelling of Zion, make full out joy, and praise; for why the Holy of Israel is great in the midst of thee.

13.1: The burden of Babylon, which burden Isaiah, the son of Amoz, saw.
13.2: Raise ye [[up]] a sign on a misty hill, and enhance ye [[the]] voice; raise ye the hand, and [[the]] dukes enter by the gates.
13.3: I have commanded to mine hallowed men, and I called my strong men in my wrath, that make full out joy in my glory.
13.4: The voice of [[the]] multitude in hills [[or mountains]], as of many peoples; the voice of [[the]] sound of kings, of heathen men gathered together. The Lord of hosts commanded to the chivalry of [[the]] battle,
13.5: to men coming from a far land. The Lord cometh from the highness of heaven, and the vessels of his strong vengeance, that he destroy all the land.
13.6: Yell ye, for the day of the Lord is nigh; as wasting, either destroying, it shall come of the Lord.
13.7: For this thing all hands shall be unmighty, and each heart of man shall fail, and shall be all-broken.
13.8: Gnawings [[or Tormentings]] and sorrows shall hold Babylonians; they shall have sorrow, as they that travail of child. Each man shall wonder at his neighbour; their cheers shall be burnt faces.
13.9: Lo! the day of the Lord shall come, cruel, and full of indignation, and of wrath, and of strong vengeance; to set the land into wilderness, and to all-break the sinners thereof from that land.
13.10: For why the stars of heaven and the shining of them shall not spread abroad their light; the sun is made dark in his rising, and the moon shall not shine in her light.
13.11: And I shall visit on the evils of the world, and I shall visit against wicked men the wickedness of them; and I shall make the pride of unfaithful men for to rest, and I shall make low the boast of strong men.
13.12: A man of full age shall be preciouser than gold, and a man shall be preciouser than pure gold and shining.
13.13: On this thing I shall trouble heaven, and the earth shall be moved from his place; for the indignation of the Lord of hosts, and for the day of wrath of his strong vengeance.
13.14: And it shall be as a doe fleeing, and as a sheep, and none shall be that shall gather together; each man shall turn to his people, and all by themselves shall flee to their land.
13.15: Each man that is found, shall be slain; and each man that cometh above, shall fall down by sword.
13.16: The young children of them shall be hurtled down before the eyes of them; their houses shall be ravished, and their wives shall be defouled.
13.17: Lo! I shall raise on them Medes, that seek not silver, neither will gold;
13.18: but they shall slay little children with arrows, and they shall not have mercy on wombs giving milk, and the eye of them shall not spare on sons.
13.19: And Babylon, that glorious city in realms, noble in the pride of Chaldees, shall be destroyed, as God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.
13.20: It shall not be inhabited till into the end, and it shall not be founded till to generation and generation; a man of Arabia shall not set tents there, and shepherds shall not rest there.
13.21: But wild beasts shall rest there, and the houses of them shall be filled with dragons; and ostriches shall dwell there, and hairy beasts shall skip there.
13.22: And bitterns shall answer there in the houses thereof, and flying serpents in the temples of lust. It is nigh that the time thereof come, and the days thereof shall not be made far;

14.1: for why the Lord shall have mercy of Jacob, and he shall choose yet of Israel, and shall make them for to rest on their land; a comeling shall be joined to them, and shall cleave to the house of Jacob.
14.2: And peoples shall hold them, and shall bring them into their place. And the house of Israel shall have them in possession into servants and hand-maids on the land of the Lord; and they shall take those men that took them, and they shall make subject their wrongful askers.
14.3: And it shall be in that day, when God shall give to thee rest of thy travail, and of thy shaking, and of hard servage, in which thou servedest before,
14.4: thou shalt take this parable against the king of Babylon, and thou shalt say, How ceased the wrongful asker, rested [[the]] tribute?
14.5: The Lord hath all-broken the staff of wicked men, the rod of lords,
14.6: that beat peoples in indignation, with uncurable wound, that subjected folks in strong vengeance, that pursued cruelly.
14.7: Each land rested, and was still; it was joyful, and made full out joy.
14.8: Also fir trees and cedars of the Lebanon were glad on thee; Since thou sleptest, none ascendeth [[or went up]] that cutteth us down.
14.9: Hell under thee is troubled for the meeting of thy coming; he shall raise giants to thee; all the princes of [[the]] earth have risen from their seats, all the princes of nations.
14.10: All they shall answer, and they shall say to thee, And thou art wounded as we, thou art made like us.
14.11: Thy pride is drawn down to hells [[or to hell]], thy dead carrion fell down; a moth shall be strewed under thee, and thy covering shall be worms.
14.12: A! Lucifer, that risedest early, how fellest thou down from heaven; thou that woundedest folks, felledest down altogether into [[the]] earth.
14.13: Which saidest in thine heart, I shall ascend [[or go up]] into heaven, I shall enhance my seat above the stars of heaven; I shall sit in the hill of testament, in the sides of the north.
14.14: I shall ascend [[or go up]] on the highness of clouds; I shall be like the Highest.
14.15: Nevertheless thou shalt be drawn down to hell, into the depth of the pit.
14.16: They that shall see thee, shall be bowed down to thee, and shall behold thee. And they shall say, Whether this is the man, that troubled [[the]] earth, that shook together realms?
14.17: that setted [[or put]] the world desert, and destroyed the cities thereof, and opened not the prison to the bound men of him?
14.18: All the kings of heathen men, all slept in glory, a man in his house.
14.19: But thou art cast out of thy sepulchre, as an unprofitable stock, as defouled with rot; and wrapped with them that be slain with sword, and went down to the foundament of the pit. As a rotten carrion,
14.20: thou shalt not have fellowship, neither with them in sepulchre, for thou hast lost thy land, thou hast slain the people; the seed of the worst men shall not be called without end.
14.21: Make ye ready his sons to slaying, for the wickedness of their fathers; they shall not rise, neither they shall inherit the land, neither they shall fill the face of the roundness of cities.
14.22: And I shall rise [[up]] on them, saith the Lord of hosts, and I shall lose the name of Babylon, and the remnants, and generation, and seed, saith the Lord.
14.23: And I shall set [[or put]] that Babylon into possession of an urchin, and into marishes of waters; and I shall sweep it with a besom, and I shall stamp, saith the Lord of hosts.
14.24: The Lord of hosts swore, saying, Whether it shall not be so, as I guessed, and it shall befall so, as I treated in soul?
14.25: That I all-break the king of Assyrians in my land, and that I defoul him in mine hills [[or my mountains]]; and his yoke shall be taken away from them, and his burden shall be taken away from the shoulder of them.
14.26: This is the counsel which I thought on all the land, and this is the hand stretched forth on all folks.
14.27: For why the Lord of hosts hath deemed, and who may make unsteadfast? and his hand is stretched forth, and who shall turn it away?
14.28: The burden of Philistines. In the year wherein king Ahaz died, this burden was made.
14.29: All thou Philistia, be not glad, for the rod of thy smiter is made less; for why a cockatrice shall go out of the root of an adder, and his seed shall swallow up a bird.
14.30: And the first engendered of poor men shall be fed, and poor men shall rest faithfully; and I shall make thy root to perish in hunger, and I shall slay thy remnants.
14.31: Yell, thou gate; cry, thou city; all Philistia is cast down; for why smoke shall come from the north, and none is that shall escape his host.
14.32: And what shall be answered to the messengers of [[the]] folk? for the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor men of his people shall hope in him.

15.1: The burden of Moab. For Ar was destroyed in night, Moab was still; for the wall was destroyed in the night, Moab was still.
15.2: The king’s house, and Dibon ascended [[or went up]] to high places, into wailing; on Nebo, and on Medeba, Moab shall yell. In all heads thereof shall be baldness, and each beard shall be shaved.
15.3: In the meeting of three ways thereof they be girded in a sackcloth, all yelling on the houses thereof, and in the streets thereof; it shall go down into weeping.
15.4: Heshbon shall cry, and Elealeh, the voice of them is heard till to Jahaz; on this thing the ready men of Moab shall yell, the soul thereof shall yell to itself.
15.5: Mine heart shall cry to Moab, the bars thereof till to Zoar, a cow calf of three years. For why a weeper shall go up by the going up of Luhith, and in the way of Horonaim they shall raise cry of sorrow [[or contrition]].
15.6: For why the waters of Nimrim shall be forsaken; for the herb dried up, burgeoning failed, all greenness perished.
15.7: By the greatness of work, and the visiting of them, to the strand [[or stream]] of sallows they shall lead them.
15.8: For why their cry compassed the end of Moab; till to Eglaim the yelling thereof, and the cry thereof till to the well of Elim.
15.9: For the waters of Dimon be filled with blood; for I shall set increasings on Dimon, to those men of Moab that fled from the lion, and to the remnants of the land.

16.1: Lord, send thou out a lamb, the lordly governor of [[the]] earth, from the stone of desert, to the hill of the daughter of Zion.
16.2: And it shall be, as a fowl flying, and birds flying away from the nest, so shall be the daughters of Moab, in the passing over of Arnon.
16.3: Take thou counsel, constrain thou counsel; set thou as night thy shadow in midday, hide thou them that flee, and betray thou not men of unsteadfast dwelling.
16.4: My fleers-away shall dwell at thee. Moab, be thou the hiding place of them from the face of the destroyer. For why dust is ended, the wretched is wasted; he that defouled the land failed.
16.5: And the king’s seat shall be made ready in mercy, and he shall sit on it in truth, in the tabernacle of David, deeming, and seeking doom, and yielding swiftly that that is just.
16.6: We have heard the pride of Moab, he is full proud; his pride, and his boast, and his indignation is more than his strength.
16.7: Therefore Moab shall yell to Moab, all Moab shall yell to them that be glad on the walls of baken tilestone; speak ye their wounds.
16.8: For why the suburbs of Heshbon and the vinery [[or vineyard]] of Sibmah be forsaken. The lords of heathen men have cut down the scions thereof; they came unto Jazer, they erred in desert. The boughs thereof be forsaken, they passed the sea.
16.9: On this thing I shall weep in the weeping of Jazer, and on the vinery [[or vineyard]] of Sibmah. Heshbon and Elealeh, I shall fill thee with my tears; for the voice of defoulers fell on thy vintage, and on thy harvest.
16.10: And gladness and full out joying shall be taken away from Carmel; and none shall make full out joy, neither shall sing heartily song in vineries [[or vineyards]]. He that was wont to wring out, shall not wring out wine in a presser [[or wine press]]; I have taken away the voice of [[the]] wringers-out.
16.11: On this thing my womb shall sound as an harp to Moab, and mine entrails to the wall of baken tilestone.
16.12: And it shall be, when it shall appear, that Moab hath travailed on his high places, it shall enter to his holy things, that it beseech, and it shall not be worthy.
16.13: This is the word which the Lord spake to Moab from that time.
16.14: And now the Lord spake, saying, In three years, that were as the years of an hired man, the glory of Moab shall be taken away on all the much people; and there shall be left in it as a little raisin, and a little, and not much.

17.1: The burden of Damascus. Lo! Damascus shall fail to be a city, and it shall be as an heap of stones in falling.
17.2: The forsaken cities of Aroer shall be to flocks; and they shall rest there, and none shall be that shall make afeared.
17.3: And help shall cease from Ephraim, and a realm from Damascus; and the remnants of Syria shall be as the glory of the sons of Israel, saith the Lord of hosts.
17.4: And it shall be, in that day, the glory of Jacob shall be made thin, and the fatness of his flesh shall fade.
17.5: And it shall be as gathering together that that is left in harvest, and his arm shall gather ears of corn, and it shall be as seeking ears of corn in the valley of Rephaim.
17.6: And there shall be left in it as a raisin, that is, a little bow, with a little fruit, and as the shaking down of the fruit of olive tree, as of two either of three olive trees in the highness of a branch, either of four or of five; in the tops thereof shall be the fruit thereof, saith the Lord God of Israel.
17.7: In that day a man shall be bowed to his maker, and his eyes shall behold to the Holy of Israel.
17.8: And he shall not be bowed to the altars, which his hands made, and which his fingers wrought; he shall not behold woods, and [[the]] temples of idols.
17.9: In that day the cities of strength thereof shall be forsaken as plows, and [[the]] corns that were forsaken of the face of the sons of Israel; and thou shalt be forsaken.
17.10: For thou hast forgotten God, thy saviour, and haddest not mind on thy strong helper; therefore thou shalt plant a faithful planting, and thou shalt sow an alien seed.
17.11: In the day of thy planting shall be a wild vine, and early thy seed shall flower; ripe corn is taken away in the day of heritage, and Israel shall make sorrow grievously.
17.12: Woe to the multitude of many peoples, as the multitude of the sea sounding, and the noise of companies as the sound of many waters.
17.13: Peoples shall sound as the sound of flowing waters, and God shall blame him; and he shall flee far, and he shall be ravished as the dust of hills [[or mountains]] from the face of the wind, and as a whirlwind before [[the]] tempest.
17.14: In the time of eventide, and lo! troubling; in the morrowtide, and he shall not abide. This is the part of them that destroyed us, and the part of them that ravished us.

18.1: Woe to the land, the cymbal of wings, which is beyond the flood of Ethiopia;
18.2: that sendeth messengers by the sea, and in vessels of papyrus on waters. Go, ye messengers, to the folk drawn up and rent; to a fearedful people, after which is none other; to the folk abiding and defouled, whose land the floods have ravished; to the hill [[or mount]] of the name of the Lord of hosts, to the hill [[or mount]] of Zion.
18.3: All ye dwellers of the world, that dwell in the land, shall see when a sign shall be raised [[up]] in the hills [[or mountains]], and ye shall hear the cry of a trump.
18.4: For why the Lord saith these things to me, I shall rest, and I shall behold in my place, as the midday light is clear, and as a cloud of dew in the day of harvest.
18.5: For why all flowered out before harvest, and unripe perfection burgeoned; and the little branches thereof shall be cut down with scythes, and those that be left, shall be cut away.
18.6: They shall be shaken out, and shall be left together to the birds of hills [[or mountains]], and to the beasts of earth; and birds shall be on him by a summer everlasting, and all the beasts of earth shall dwell by winter on him.
18.7: In that time a gift shall be brought to the Lord of hosts, of the people drawn up and rent; of the people fearedful, after which was none other; of the folk abiding and defouled, whose land floods ravished; the gift shall be brought to the place of the name of the Lord of hosts, to the hill [[or mount]] of Zion.

19.1: The burden of Egypt. Lo! the Lord shall ascend on a light cloud, and he shall enter into Egypt; and the simulacra of Egypt shall be moved from his face, and the heart of Egypt shall fail in the midst thereof.
19.2: And I shall make Egyptians to run together against Egyptians, and a man shall fight against his brother, and a man against his friend, a city against a city, and a realm against a realm.
19.3: And the spirit of Egypt shall be broken in the entrails thereof, and I shall cast down the counsel thereof; and they shall ask their simulacra, and their false diviners, and their men that have unclean spirits speaking in the womb, and their diviners by sacrifices made on altars to fiends.
19.4: And I shall betake Egypt into the hand of cruel lords, and a strong king shall be lord of them, saith the Lord God of hosts.
19.5: And [[the]] water of the sea shall wax dry, and the flood shall be desolate, and shall be dried.
19.6: And the floods shall fail, and the strands [[or rivers]] of the fields shall be made thin, and shall be dried; a reed and spire shall fade.
19.7: The bottom of water shall be made naked, and streams from their wells; and the moist place of all seed shall be dried, it shall wax dry, and it shall not be.
19.8: And [[the]] fishers shall mourn, and all that cast hook into the flood shall wail; and they that spread abroad a net on the face of waters shall fade.
19.9: They shall be shamed, that wrought flax, folding and ordaining subtle things.
19.10: And the water places thereof shall be dry; all that made ponds to take fishes, shall be shamed.
19.11: The fond princes [[or fools]] of Tanis, the wise counsellors of Pharaoh, gave unwise counsel; how shall ye say to Pharaoh, I am the son of wise men, the son of eld [[or old]] kings?
19.12: Where be now thy wise men? Tell they to thee, and show they, what the Lord of hosts thought on Egypt.
19.13: The princes of Tanis be made fools; the princes of Memphis faded; they deceived Egypt, a cornerstone of the peoples thereof.
19.14: The Lord meddled [[or mingled]] a spirit of error in the midst thereof; and they made Egypt for to err in all his work, as a drunken man and spewing erreth.
19.15: And work shall not be to Egypt, that it make an head and tail bowing and refraining.
19.16: In that day Egypt shall be as women, and they shall be astonied, and shall dread of the face of the moving of the hand of the Lord of hosts, which he moved on it.
19.17: And the land of Judah shall be to Egypt into dread; each that shall think on it, shall dread of the face of the counsel of the Lord of hosts, which he thought on it.
19.18: In that day five cities shall be in the land of Egypt, and shall speak with the tongue of Canaan, and shall swear by the Lord of hosts; the city of the sun shall be called one.
19.19: In that day the altar of the Lord shall be in the midst of the land of Egypt, and the title of the Lord shall be beside the end thereof;
19.20: and it shall be into a sign and witnessing to the Lord of hosts, in the land of Egypt. For they shall cry to the Lord from the face of the troubler, and he shall send a saviour to them, and a for-fighter, that shall deliver them.
19.21: And the Lord shall be known of Egypt, and [[the]] Egyptians shall know the Lord in that day; and they shall worship him in sacrifices and gifts, and they shall make vows to the Lord, and they shall pay.
19.22: And the Lord shall smite Egypt with a wound, and shall make it whole; and [[the]] Egyptians shall turn again to the Lord, and he shall be pleased in them, and he shall make them whole.
19.23: In that day a way shall be from Egypt into Assyrians, and Egyptians shall serve Assur; and Assur shall enter into Egypt, and Egypt into Assyrians.
19.24: In that day Israel shall be the third to Egypt and to Assur, the blessing in the middle of [[the]] earth;
19.25: whom the Lord of hosts blessed, saying, Blessed be my people of Egypt, and the work of mine hands be to Assyrians; but mine heritage be to Israel.

20.1: In the year wherein Tartan entered into Ashdod, when Sargon, the king of Assyrians, had sent him, and he had fought against Ashdod, and had taken it;
20.2: in that time the Lord spake in the hand of Isaiah, the son of Amoz, and said, Go thou, and unbind the sack-cloth from thy loins, and take away thy shoes from thy feet. And he did so, going naked and unshod.
20.3: And the Lord said, As my servant Isaiah went naked and unshod, a sign and great wonder of three years shall be on Egypt, and on Ethiopia;
20.4: so the king of Assyrians shall drive the captivity of Egypt, and the passing over of Ethiopia, a young man and an eld [[or old]] man, naked and unshod, with the buttocks uncovered, to the shame of Egypt.
20.5: And they shall dread, and shall be ashamed of Ethiopia, their hope, and of Egypt, their glory.
20.6: And a dweller of this isle shall say on that day, This was our hope, to which we fled for help, that they should deliver us from the face of the king of Assyrians; and how may we escape?

21.1: The burden of the forsaken sea. As whirlwinds come from the south-west, it cometh from [[the]] desert, from the horrible land.
21.2: An hard revelation is told to me; he that is unfaithful, doeth unfaithfully; and he that is a destroyer, destroyeth. Thou Elam, go up, and thou Media, beseech [[or besiege]]; I made all the wailing thereof for to cease.
21.3: Therefore my loins be filled with sorrow; anguish wielded me, as the anguish of a woman travailing of child; I fell down, when I heard; I was troubled, when I saw.
21.4: Mine heart faded, darknesses astonied me; Babylon, my darling, is set [[or put]] to me into miracle.
21.5: Set thou a board, behold thou into a looking place; rise, ye princes, eating and drinking, take ye [[the]] shield.
21.6: For why the Lord said these things to me, Go thou, and set a looker; and tell he, whatever thing he seeth.
21.7: And he saw the chariot of two horsemen, the rider of an ass, and the rider of a camel; and he beheld diligently with much looking,
21.8: and [[he]] cried as a lion, I stand continually by day on the looking place of the Lord, and I stand by all nights on my keeping.
21.9: Lo! this cometh, a man-rider of a cart of horsemen. And Isaiah cried, and said, Babylon fell down, fell down; and all the graven images of gods thereof be all-broken into [[the]] earth.
21.10: My threshing, and the daughter of my cornfloor, I have told to you what things I heard of the Lord of hosts, of God of Israel.
21.11: The burden of Dumah. It crieth from Seir to me, Keeper, what hour of the night? keeper, what hour of the night?
21.12: The keeper said, The morrowtide cometh, and night; if ye seek, seek ye, and be ye converted, and come ye.
21.13: The burden of Arabia. In the forest at eventide ye shall sleep, in the paths of Dedanim.
21.14: Ye that dwell in the land of the south, run, and bear water to the thirsty; and run ye with loaves to him that fleeth.
21.15: For they fled from the face of swords, from the face of [[the]] sword nighing, from the face of [[the]] bow bent, from the face of [[the]] grievous battle.
21.16: For the Lord saith these things to me, Yet in one year, as in the year of an hired man, and all the glory of Kedar shall be taken away.
21.17: And the remnants of the number of strong archers of the sons of Kedar shall be made less; for why the Lord God of Israel spake.

22.1: The burden of the valley of vision. What also is to thee, for and all thou ascendedest [[or wentest up]] into [[the]] roofs,
22.2: thou full of cry, a city of much people, a city full out joying? thy slain men were not slain by sword, neither thy dead men were dead in battle.
22.3: All thy princes fled together, and were bound hard; all that were found, were bound together, they fled far.
22.4: Therefore I said, Go ye away from me, I shall weep bitterly; do not ye be busy to comfort me on the destroying of the daughter of my people.
22.5: For why a day of slaying, and of defouling, and of weepings, is ordained of the Lord God of hosts, in the valley of vision; and he searcheth the wall, and is worshipful on the hill [[or the mountain]].
22.6: And Elam took an arrow case, or a quiver, and the chariot of an horseman; and the shield made naked the wall.
22.7: And thy chosen valleys, Jerusalem, shall be full of carts; and knights shall put their seats in the gate.
22.8: And the covering of Judah shall be showed; and thou shalt see in that day the place of armours of the house of the forest;
22.9: and ye shall see the crazings of the city of David, for those be multiplied. Ye gathered together the waters of the lower cistern,
22.10: and ye numbered the houses of Jerusalem, and ye destroyed [[the]] houses, to make strong the wall;
22.11: and ye made a pit betwixt two walls, and ye restored the water of the eld [[or old]] cistern; and ye beheld not to him, that made that Jerusalem, and ye saw not the worker thereof afar.
22.12: And the Lord of hosts shall call in that day to weeping, and to mourning, and to baldness, and to a girdle of sackcloth;
22.13: and lo! joy and gladness is to slay calves, and to strangle wethers, to eat flesh, and to drink wine; eat we, and drink we, for we shall die tomorrow.
22.14: And the voice of the Lord of hosts is showed in mine ears, This wicked-ness shall not be forgiven to you, till ye die, saith the Lord God of hosts.
22.15: The Lord God of hosts saith these things, Go thou, and enter to him that dwelleth in the tabernacle, to Shebna, the sovereign of the temple; and thou shalt say to him,
22.16: What thou here, either as who here? for thou hast hewed [[out]] to thee a sepulchre here, thou hast hewed a memorial in high place diligently, a tabernacle in a stone to thee.
22.17: Lo! the Lord shall make thee to be borne out, as a capon is borne out, and as a cloth, so he shall raise thee.
22.18: He crowning shall crown thee with tribulation; he shall send thee as a ball into a large land and wide; there thou shalt die, and there shall be the chariot of thy glory, and the shame of the house of thy Lord.
22.19: And I shall cast thee out of thy standing, and I shall put thee down of thy service.
22.20: And it shall be, in that day I shall call my servant Eliakim, the son of Hilkiah;
22.21: and I shall clothe him in thy coat, and I shall comfort him with thy girdle, and I shall give thy power into the hands of him; and he shall be as a father to them that dwell in Jeru-salem, and to the house of Judah.
22.22: And I shall give the key of the house of David on his shoulder; and he shall open, and none shall be that shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall be that shall open.
22.23: And I shall set him a stake, either a perch, in a faithful place, and he shall be into a seat of glory of the house of his father.
22.24: And thou shalt hang on him all the glory of the house of his father, diverse kinds of vessels, each little vessel, from the vessels of cups, till to each vessel of musics.
22.25: In that day, saith the Lord of hosts, the stake that was set [[or fixed]] in the faithful place, shall be taken away, and it shall be broken, and shall fall down; and shall perish that hanged therein, for the Lord spake.

23.1: The burden of Tyre. Ye ships of the sea, yell, for the house is destroyed, from whence comfort was wont to come; from the land of Chittim, and [[it]] was showed to them.
23.2: Be ye still, that dwell in the isle, the merchants of Sidon; [[the]] men passing [[over]] the sea filled thee in many waters;
23.3: the seed of Nile is [[the]] harvest, the flood is the corn thereof, and it is made the merchandise of heathen men.
23.4: Thou, Sidon, be ashamed, said the sea, the strength of the sea, and said, I travailed not of child, and I childed not, and I nourished not young men, and I brought not fully virgins to increasing.
23.5: When it shall be heard in Egypt, they shall make sorrow, when they hear of Tyre.
23.6: Pass ye the seas; yell ye, that dwell in the isle.
23.7: Whether this city is not yours, that had glory from eld days in his eldness? the feet thereof shall lead it [[a]] far, to go in pilgrimage.
23.8: Who thought this thing on Tyre, sometime crowned, whose merchants were princes, the sellers of merchandise thereof were noble men of [[the]] earth?
23.9: The Lord of hosts thought this thing, that he should draw down the pride of all glory, and that he should bring to shame all the noble men of earth.
23.10: Thou daughter of the sea, pass [[over]] thy land as a flood; a girdle is no more to thee.
23.11: It stretched forth his hand above the sea, and troubled realms. The Lord sent against Canaan, for to all-break the strong men thereof;
23.12: and he said, Thou maiden, the daughter of Sidon, that sufferest challenge, shalt no more add, that thou have glory. Rise thou, and pass over the sea into Chittim; there also no rest shall be to thee.
23.13: Lo! the land of Chaldees, such a people was not; Assur founded that Tyre; they led over into captivity the strong men thereof; they [[under]] mined the houses thereof; they setted [[or put]] it into falling.
23.14: Yell, ye ships of the sea, for your strength be destroyed.
23.15: And it shall be, in that day, thou, Tyre, shalt be in forgetting by seventy years, as the days of one king; but after seventy years, as the song of a whore shall be to Tyre.
23.16: Thou whore, given to forgetting, take an harp, compass the city; sing thou well, use thou oft a song, that mind be of thee.
23.17: And it shall be, after seventy years, the Lord shall visit Tyre, and shall bring it again to his hire; and again it shall be, when it shall do fornication with all [[the]] realms of [[the]] earth, on the face of [[the]] earth.
23.18: And the merchandises thereof and the meeds thereof shall be hallowed to the Lord; they shall not be hid, neither shall be laid up; for why the merchandise thereof shall be to them that dwell before the Lord, that they eat to fullness, and be clothed till to eldness [[or oldness]].

24.1: Lo! the Lord shall destroy the earth, and shall make it naked, and shall torment the face thereof; and he shall scatter abroad the dwellers thereof.
24.2: And it shall be, as the people, so the priest; as the servant, so his lord; as the handmaid, so the lady of her; as a buyer, so he that selleth; as the lender, so he that taketh borrowing; as he that asketh again, so he that oweth.
24.3: By destroying the land shall be destroyed, and shall be made naked by ravishing; for why the Lord spake this word.
24.4: The earth mourned, and floated away, and is made sick; the world floated away, the highness of the people of [[the]] earth is made sick,
24.5: and the earth is slain of his dwellers. For they passed [[the]] laws, changed [[the]] right, destroyed [[the]] everlasting bond of peace.
24.6: For this thing, cursing shall devour the earth, and the dwellers thereof shall do sin; and therefore the lovers thereof shall be mad, and few men shall be left.
24.7: [[The]] Vintage mourned, the vine is sick; all men that were glad in heart wailed.
24.8: The joy of tympans ceased, the sound of glad men rested; the sweet-ness of [[the]] harp with song was stilled.
24.9: They shall not drink wine; a bitter drink shall be to them that shall drink it.
24.10: The city of vanity is all-broken; each house is closed, for no man entereth.
24.11: Cry shall be on wine in [[the]] streets, all gladness is forsaken, the joy of [[the]] earth is taken away.
24.12: Desolation is left in the city, and wretchedness shall oppress the gates.
24.13: For these things shall be in the midst of [[the]] earth, in the midst of peoples, as if a few fruits of olive trees that be left be shaken off from the olive tree, and raisins, when the vintage is ended.
24.14: These men shall raise [[up]] their voice, and shall praise, when the Lord shall be glorified; they shall show signs of gladness from the sea.
24.15: For this thing glorify ye the Lord in teachings; in the isles of the sea glorify ye the name of the Lord God of Israel.
24.16: From the ends of [[the]] earth we have heard praisings, the glory of the just [[or the rightwise]]. And I said, My private to me, my private to me. Woe to me, [[the]] trespassers have trespassed, and have trespassed by [[the]] trespassing of breakers of the law.
24.17: Fearedfulness, and a ditch, and a snare on thee, that art a dweller of [[the]] earth.
24.18: And it shall be, he that shall flee from the face of fearedfulness, shall fall into the ditch; and he that shall deliver himself from the ditch, shall be holden of the snare; for why the windows of high things be opened, and the foundaments of [[the]] earth shall be shaken together.
24.19: The earth shall be broken with breaking, the earth shall be defouled with defouling, the earth shall be moved with moving,
24.20: the earth shall be shaken with shaking, as a drunken man. And it shall be taken away, as the tabernacle of one night, and the wickedness thereof shall grieve it; and it shall fall down, and it shall not add, for to rise again.
24.21: And it shall be, in that day the Lord shall visit on the knighthood of heaven on high, and on the kings of earth, that be on earth.
24.22: And they shall be gathered together in the gathering together of a bundle into the pit, and they shall be enclosed there in prison; and after many days they shall be visited.
24.23: And the moon shall be ashamed, and the sun shall be confounded, when the Lord of hosts shall reign in the hill of Zion, and in Jerusalem, and shall be glorified in the sight of his elder men.

25.1: Lord, thou art my God, I shall enhance thee, and I shall acknowledge to thy name; for thou hast done marvels, thine eld [[or old]] faithful thoughts. Amen.
25.2: For thou hast set the city into a burial, a strong city into falling, the house of aliens, that it be not a city, and be not builded without end.
25.3: For this thing a strong people shall praise thee, the city of strong folks shall dread thee.
25.4: For thou art made strength to a poor man, strength to a needy man in his tribulation, hope from [[the]] whirlwind, a shadowing place from heat; for why the spirit of strong men is as a whirlwind hurling the wall.
25.5: As by heat in thirst, thou shalt make meek the noise of aliens; and as by heat under a cloud burning, thou shalt make the scions of strong men to fade.
25.6: And the Lord of hosts shall make in this hill to all peoples the feast of fat things, the feast of vintage of fat things full of marrow, of vintage well-refined.
25.7: And he shall cast down in this hill the face of [[the]] bond, bound altogether on all peoples, and the web which he weaved on all nations.
25.8: And he shall cast down death [[into]] without end, and the Lord God shall do away each tear from each face; and he shall do away the shame of his people from each land, for the Lord spake.
25.9: And they shall say in that day, Lo! this is our God; we abided him, and he shall save us; this is the Lord; we suffered him, and we shall make full out joy, and shall be glad in his health.
25.10: For why the hand of the Lord shall rest in this hill, and Moab shall be threshed under him, as chaffs be stamped in a wain.
25.11: And he shall stretch forth his hands under him, as a swimmer stretcheth forth to swim; and he shall make low the glory of him with [[the]] hurtling down of his hands.
25.12: And the strongholds of thine high walls shall fall down, and shall be made low, and shall be drawn down to the earth, till to the dust.

26.1: In that day this song shall be sung in the land of Judah. The city of our strength; the saviour shall be set therein, the wall and the forewall, either a stronghold before the wall.
26.2: Open ye the gates, and the just [[or rightwise]] folk shall enter, keeping truth.
26.3: The eld [[or old]] error is gone away; thou shalt keep peace, peace, for thou, Lord, we hoped in thee.
26.4: Ye have hoped in the Lord, in everlasting worlds, in the Lord God, strong without end.
26.5: For he shall bow down them that dwell on high, and he shall make low an high city; he shall make it low till to the earth; he shall draw it down till to the dust.
26.6: The foot of a poor man shall defoul it, and the steps of needy men shall defoul it.
26.7: The way of a just man is rightful, the path of a just man is rightful to go. [[The way of the rightwise is even, even the path of the rightwise to go.]]
26.8: And in the way of thy dooms, Lord, we suffered thee; thy name, and thy memorial is in desire of soul.
26.9: My soul shall desire thee in the night, but also with my spirit in mine entrails; from the morrowtide I shall wake to thee. When thou shalt make thy dooms in [[the]] earth, all dwellers of the world shall learn rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]].
26.10: Do we mercy to the wicked man, and he shall not learn to do rightwise-ness; in the land of saints he did wicked things, and he shall not see the glory of the Lord.
26.11: Lord, thine hand be enhanced, that they see not; peoples having envy see, and be shamed, and fire devour thine enemies.
26.12: Lord, thou shalt give peace to us, for thou hast wrought all our works in us.
26.13: Our Lord God, lords had us in possession, without thee; only in thee have we mind of thy name.
26.14: They that die, live not, and giants, rise not again. Therefore thou hast visited, and hast all-broken them, and thou hast lost all the mind of them;
26.15: and Lord, thou hast forgiven to a folk, thou hast forgiven to a folk. Whether thou art glorified? thou hast made far from thee all the ends of [[the]] earth.
26.16: Lord, in anguish they sought thee; in the tribulation of grutching, thy doctrine to them.
26.17: As she that conceived, when she nigheth sorrowful to the child bearing, crieth in her sorrows, so we be made, Lord, of thy face.
26.18: We have conceived, and we have as travailed of child, and we have childed the spirit of health; we did not rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]] in earth. Therefore the dwellers of [[the]] earth fell not down;
26.19: thy dead men shall live, and my slain men shall rise again. Ye that dwell in dust, awake, and praise; for why the dew of light is thy dew, and thou shalt draw down the land of giants into falling.
26.20: Go thou, my people, enter into thy beds, close thy doors on thee, be thou hid a little at a moment, till indignation pass.
26.21: For lo! the Lord shall go out of his place, to visit the wickedness of the dwellers of [[the]] earth against him; and the earth shall show his blood, and shall no more cover his slain men.

27.1: In that day the Lord shall visit in his hard sword, and great, and strong, on leviathan, serpent, a bar [[or a lever]], and on leviathan, the crooked serpent; and he shall slay the whale, which is in the sea.
27.2: In that day the vinery [[or the vineyard]] of clean wine and good shall sing to him.
27.3: I am the Lord that keep that vinery; suddenly I shall give drink to it, lest peradventure it be visited against it; night and day I keep it,
27.4: indignation is not to me. Who shall give me a thorn and [[a]] briar? In battle I shall go on it, I shall burn it altogether.
27.5: Whether rather I shall hold my strength? It shall make peace to me, it shall make peace to me,
27.6: for the merit of them that shall go out with fierceness from Jacob. Israel shall flower and bring forth seed, and they shall fill the face of the world with seed.
27.7: Whether he smote it by the wound of the people of Jews smiting him? either as it killed the slain men of him, so it was slain?
27.8: In measure against measure, when it shall be cast away, he shall deem it; he bethought in his hard spirit, by the day of heat.
27.9: Therefore on this thing wickedness shall be forgiven to the house of Jacob, and this shall be all the fruit, that the sin thereof be done away, when it hath set all the stones of the altar as the stones of ashes hurtled down. Woods and temples shall not stand.
27.10: Forsooth the strong city shall be desolate, the fair city shall be left, and shall be forsaken as a desert; there a calf shall be pastured, and shall lie there, and shall waste the highness thereof.
27.11: In the dryness of ripe corn thereof women coming, and they that teach it, shall be all-broken. Forsooth it is not a wise people; therefore he that made it, shall not have mercy on it, and he that formed it, shall not spare it.
